Rarely has the war within been portrayed as wrenchingly and as riotously as it is in director Trent Stork's fiendishly funny revival of “Hand to God,” a dark dramedy by Robert Askins that opened Wednesday at Paramount's Copley Theatre.
"Hand to God” is a deeply funny, foul-mouthed play about grief and the necessity of devils.
Six years ago I said that this play is a MUST SEE! Let me repeat myself- "this production is a Must See and worth the trip to Aurora! This is an amazing story about people and their lives.
Paramount is knocking it out of the park with this series.

cn.t: Critics praise this darkly comic production for its fiendishly funny performances and bold exploration of inner turmoil through puppetry, with the cast earning particular acclaim for their tour de force work in this irreverent, provocative play.
